 2. lamina Bank Limited filed Artha Rin Case No.300 of 2008 before the learned 

 District Judge, Dhaka and subsequently renumbered as Artha Rin Case No.149 of 2009 when transferred to Artha Rin Adalat, 40 Court, Dhaka for realization of Tk. 18,23,59,000/- against defendant opposite party Nos.1 and 3-8. On contested hearing against defendant No.2, some of the defendants did not contest. Decree was passed on 25.05.2010 and Money Execution Case being Artha Zari Case No.01 of 2011 was filed on 01.06.2010. 

 3. 30 party petitioners filed present Miscellaneous case on 14.04.2011 stating that the decree was passed against wrong person and 3' party petitioners is actual owner of the suit property and decree was passed fraudulently on the averments made in the plaint. The court fixed date after date in taking step for submitting schedule as per Section 32(2) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain which having not been filed or submitted the case was dismissed. 

 4. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Sadananda Rana, learned Advocates, appearing for the applicants-petitioners, on reference to the case of Mollah Shahidul Islam Vs. Monsur Rahman, 57 DLR 164 = 21 BLD 171 submits that, fraud has been alleged having been pleaded and exposed, as security or assurance as contemplated under 32(2) of the Ain are not required to furnish or deposited. 

 Ors Vs. Govt. of Bangladesh & Ors 23BLI(HCD) 2015 Code of Civil Procedure. The investigation of claim and only objection to that claim are dealt with by rule 58 to rule 62 and beyond that no third party's claim is conceivable under any provision of Order XXI. The provision of investigation of claims and objections has been clearly provided under the aforesaid rules under heading 'investigation of claims and objections' and the claim is preferred when the• property is under the attachment. The petitioner in the instant case although apparently made claim over the property auction sold, but in substance they have challenged the auction sale proceeding on the ground of fraud. So the kind of claim that has been preferred does not come within the ambit of rule 58 of Order XXI of the CPC. It is further indicated in sub-section ( I ) of Section 32 of the Ain, 2003 that the decree holder also may file objection within the period not exceeding 30 days and can claim hearing for disposal of the claim made by the 3"I party. Therefore, the contemplation of the legislature in Section 32(2) is the investigation of claims and objection as provided under Order XXI, Rule 58 not beyond the periphery of rule 58, and since the petitioner filed the petition under Order XXI Rule 90 and 91 for setting aside the sale on the ground of fraud they are not required furnish any security as provided under subsection 2 of Section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The teamed Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat appeared to have exercised his power and jurisdiction beyond the law."
